title: Health-ring pulse is 16x slower than documented: step divisors 16/8 yield 0.078/0.156 Hz, not the claimed 1.25/2.5 Hz (art-direction §6.1)
evidence:
+pulse_factor :: proc(tick: u64, node_id: u32, step: u32) -> f32 {
+	table := PULSE16 // local copy — a constant can't be indexed by a runtime index
+	idx := (tick + u64(node_id) * 5) / u64(step) & 15
+	return table[idx]
+}
+	step: u32 = 16 // slow amber pulse ~1.25 Hz @ 20 Hz logic
+		step = 8 // fast critical pulse ~2.5 Hz
+// the per-state rate (amber 1 tick/step = 1.25 Hz, red 2 ticks/step = 2.5 Hz
+// at 20 Hz — the art-direction §6.1 slow/fast language).
+  itself the escalation signal: slow ~1.2 Hz strained, fast ~2.5 Hz critical).
detail: idx advances once per `step` ticks; the 16-entry envelope takes 16xstep ticks = 256 (amber) / 128 (red) = 0.078/0.156 Hz, while the comments and art-direction §6.1 claim 1.25/2.5 Hz — 16x slower.
recommended_fix: Advance the index every tick for amber (divisor 1) and 2 steps/tick for red (e.g. (tick*2 + off) / 1 & 15) so cycles are 16/8 ticks; or correct the comments and §6.1 claim.

title: Negative lead-time JSON values bypass the 'leads > 0' fail-fast via u64 wrap
evidence:
+			b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_strained_lead_ticks", 0))
+			b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_critical_lead_ticks", 0))
+			b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "pipe_pressure_lead_ticks", 0))
+		if b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks == 0 || b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks == 0 ||
+			b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks == 0 {
detail: u64(jint(...)) wraps a negative JSON lead to a huge u64, so the `== 0` rejection never fires; a negative lead passes fail-fast, then clamps the forecast window to tick 0 — a lie about the reaction window.
recommended_fix: Validate the signed integer before conversion (if lead <= 0 return the named error), then convert to u64 only after passing.
